text:
jamie: FYI posted a short follow-up from the checkpointing RFC — proposing a deterministic checkpoint-first upgrade flow for air-gapped installs. https://rfd.redwood/internal/rfc/checkpoint-first :eyes:

jamie: TL;DR: create signed, content-addressed checkpoint snapshots, publish delta manifests that are applied on top. Operator applies checkpoint locally, then transactionally activates components.

deepa: quick q — how do we handle partial failures during activation? operator crash halfway, disks full, etc.

jamie: good call. plan is a two-phase apply: 
1) preflight verify (enough disk, signatures OK, deps resolved)
2) staged extract (write to temp area)
3) activation swap (atomic rename/symlink)
if activation fails, revert by re-pointing symlink to previous checkpoint.

mike: re: symlink swap, slightly worried about processes holding file descriptors into old files. we should include a post-activation drain step and an operator flag to force-kill after timeout.

nisha: +1. also we need observability hooks: operator should emit metrics: checkpoint.fetch.duration, staged.extract.bytes, activation.swap.success, revert.count, last-failure-reason. tie to per-cluster traces so customers see exact stage.

jamie: agreed on metrics. adding: we will include a small JSON preflight report alongside every checkpoint: {"size":...,"requires_reboot":false,"estimated_apply_time_s":...} — operator surfaces it in UI.

deepa: how are deltas represented? full tarball vs file-level diffs? for air-gapped we care about minimal transfer.

jamie: delta manifest supports two modes: 
- chunked blobs (content-addressed chunks, deduped across checkpoints)
- overlay layer diffs for small metadata-only changes
Operator chooses chunked mode by default. we expect most customers will seed a large base checkpoint once and then apply small chunked deltas.

mike: signing/attestation model? must be easy for offline operators.

jamie: checkpoint bundles are signed by the release-signing key. for air-gapped installs we support two verification modes: 
- online verifier (default hosted KMS signature verification)
- offline verifier: supplies a signed attest chain blob that the operator can validate with a local public key bundle. we will publish a small verify-cli that runs offline checks and prints a deterministic result.

nisha: what about rollback primitives? automatic vs manual?

jamie: prefer guarded manual rollback. automatic rollback only for a narrow set: if activation swap fails persistently or if healthchecks fail within a short window. otherwise operator leaves reverted state and surface reason. arch-sig: any strong opinions?

arch-sig: prefer explicit failures over heuristics. auto-rollback tends to hide root cause. allow configurable auto-rollback threshold but default to manual. :thumbsup:

deepa: operator UX: if someone applies a delta and then wants to rebase to a different checkpoint (e.g., new base image), how do we make that efficient offline?

jamie: we surface a rebase command that will compute a local three-way merge between current checkpoint, target base, and delta manifest. it favors content-addressed chunks and will fetch only missing chunks. offline mode accepts an attached seed bundle on USB.

mike: curious about storage layout. are we keeping entire historical checkpoints locally? that's expensive.

jamie: operator keeps N last checkpoints by default (configurable). storage reclamation runs asynchronously and keeps metrics. we also support compacted manifests that allow reconstructing intermediate states from chunk graph.

nisha: please add a metric for compact/GC reclaim failures. customers often hit GC bugs late.

jamie: will add. also proposing an emergency-apply small command: `rwd-operator emergency-apply --standalone <bundle.tar>` which bypasses manifest resolution when operators only have a single signed bundle. docs will warn loud about this.

deploy-bot: CI: rfc/checkpoint-first tests: unit 112 passed, integration 7/9 (two flaky network sims) — see https://ci.redwood/reports/5143219876

mike: we should add a runtime health probe API that each component can register: `/internal/upgrade-health` returning JSON stage status. then operator can query before switching traffic.

deepa: agree. also provide a dry-run apply mode that exits with nonzero if any post-activation checks would fail.

jamie: good notes. next steps: I’ll update the RFC to include: preflight JSON schema, operator state machine diagram, metrics set, and offline verifier CLI usage. will push a PR by EOD. volunteers to review?

nisha: can review metrics + health probes.

mike: will take rollback and process-drain wording.

deepa: I’ll iterate on operator UX and rebase command docs.

jamie: awesome. thanks y'all. tagging follow-up meeting: Thu 10am PT. :calendar: 

arch-sig: approved to proceed with checkpoint-first prototype. please keep the prototype small and test heavy.

jamie: noted — prototype will be minimal, focusing on atomic swap + preflight + verify-cli.

mike: one more nit — ensure our atomic swap works on both ext4 and xfs (and note caveat for NFS mounts). add test matrix.

jamie: added to the PR checklist.

deploy-bot: scheduled: prototype branch created rwd/checkpoint-proto-5143219876

jamie: thanks, closing thread for now. we’ll reopen if blockers show up. :white_check_mark:
